Let ⊔i=1kE(ai,bi)⊔i=1k′E(ai′,bi′)⊔i=1k′′E(ai′′,bi′′)⊔i=1k(3)E(ai(3),bi(3))↪𝜑ℙ2\displaystyle\sqcup_{i=1}^{k}E(a_{i},b_{i})\sqcup_{i=1}^{k^{\prime}}E(a_{i}^{\prime},b_{i}^{\prime})\sqcup_{i=1}^{k^{\prime\prime}}E(a_{i}^{\prime\prime},b_{i}^{\prime\prime})\sqcup_{i=1}^{k^{(3)}}E(a_{i}^{(3)},b_{i}^{(3)})\overset{\varphi}{\hookrightarrow}\mathbb{P}^{2} be a symplectic embedding, which is the restriction of an embedding of the disjoint union of closed ellipsoids, and let CC an immersed,

The main result of this paper is a solution to the homological Arnold conjecture over ℤ{\mathbb{Z}} for arbitrary closed symplectic manifolds. This bound is similar to the Morse inequality over ℤ{\mathbb{Z}} which takes into account the torsion part of the homology.
Theorem A.
Let (M,ω)(M,\omega) be a closed symplectic manifold with minimal Chern number NN. Suppose H:S1×M→ℝH:S^{1}\times M\to{\mathbb{R}} is a nondegenerate 11-periodic Hamiltonian. Then the number of 11-periodic orbits of HH is bounded below by
rank ​H∗​(M,ℚ)+2​∑i∈ℤ/2​Nτi(2​N)​(M).\text{rank }H_{*}(M;{\mathbb{Q}})+2\sum_{i\in{\mathbb{Z}}/2N}\tau_{i}^{(2N)}(M).
(1.1)
We briefly comment on the historical background of the Arnold conjecture. Arnold conjectured ([Arn78, Appendix 9], [Arn65]) that the number of 11-periodic orbits of any nondegenerate Hamiltonian is at least the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function on MM (the strong Arnold conjecture) and suggested that it is a consequence of a version of Morse inequality. While the strong Arnold conjecture is difficult to prove, there have been significant progresses towards the homological Arnold conjecture, namely, the number of periodic orbits being bounded from below by the total Betti number.11
1
From now on, in this paper, the Arnold conjecture refers to the homological version. These progresses started with the breakthrough of Conley–Zehnder [CZ83], who solved the strong Arnold conjecture for T2​nT^{2n} using finite dimensional methods. Conley–Zehnder’s method was later extended by Floer to solve the strong Arnold conjecture for surfaces with genus at least 22 and for certain classes of Kähler manifolds [Flo86]. It was then followed by the revolutionary work of Floer [Flo89] which invented the Floer homology and established the Arnold conjecture for (M,ω)(M,\omega) satisfying [ω]=λ​c1​(M)[\omega]=\lambda c_{1}(M) for some λ∈ℝ\lambda\in{\mathbb{R}} (monotone symplectic manifolds). Floer’s result was extended by Hofer–Salamon [HS95] and Ono [Ono95] to cover all semi-positive symplectic manifolds, i.e., (M2​n,ω)(M^{2n},\omega) which does not have A∈π2​(M)A\in\pi_{2}(M) such that ω⁡(A)>0\omega(A)>0 and 3−n≤c1​(A)<03-n\leq c_{1}(A)<0. It is worth noting that these results hold over ℤ\mathbb{Z}.
For general symplectic manifolds, Fukaya–Ono[FO99], Liu–Tian[LT98b], and Ruan [Rua99] proved the homological Arnold conjecture with lower bound coming from the rational total Betti number. These papers are based on a kind of abstract machinery, generally called the “virtual technique,” which is designed for generalizing Floer’s construction (along side with the mathematical theory of Gromov–Witten invariants). The most recent advancement towards the homological Arnold conjecture by Abouzaid–Blumberg [AB21], which relies more heavily on stable homotopy theory, bounds the number of periodic orbits from below by the sum of Betti numbers in any finite field. In addition to the aforementioned works, using different versions of the virtual technique, the weak Arnold conjecture over rational numbers is reproved in [Par16] and [FW22].
Theorem A allows one to obtain a sharper lower bound for the number of 11-periodic orbits of a given non-degenerate Hamiltonian by treating the torsion components of H∗​(M,ℤ)H_{*}(M;\mathbb{Z}) uniformly and simultaneously. The lower bound provided by rank​H∗​(M,𝔽p){\rm rank}H_{*}(M;\mathbb{F}_{p}) as from [AB21] is also recovered from Theorem A by the universal coefficient theorem. Our bound is also strictly stronger than the bound of Abouzaid–Blumberg, for example, when Heven​(M)H_{\rm even}(M) has only pp-torsion and Hodd​(M)H_{\rm odd}(M) has only qq-torsion and p≠qp\neq q.

purpose: Current PSS/isomorphism and cyclic bound
text: Continuing our previous work on the integral Arnold conjecture [14], we establish the foundation of Hamiltonian Floer theory over integer coefficients on any compact symplectic manifold. This package produces a well-defined chain homotopy class of Floer complexes, chain-level continuation maps, the Piunikhin–Salamon–Schwarz (PSS) isomorphism, and an associative pair-of-pants product. When the Hamiltonian is the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration for a prime number 𝗉{\sf p}, we also establish the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant Floer theory in characteristic 𝗉{\sf p}, including the equivariant Floer complex and the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant pair-of-pants product. Moreover, we define quantum Steenrod operations for any compact symplectic manifold and compare them with the equivariant pair-of-pants products via the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant PSS map. We also obtain chain-level invariants such as spectral numbers and barcodes and prove quantitative properties of the equivariant pair-of-pants product.

text:
So for which Legendrians is tube torsion defined? A particularly elusive class of Legendrians is given by the Legendrian lifts of nearby Lagrangians. We recall that for LL and MM closed, connected, smooth nn-dimensional manifolds, a nearby Lagrangian is an exact Lagrangian embedding L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M. A nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M admits a generating function on some tube bundle if and only if the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O is nullhomotopic [ACGK]. Therefore the tube torsion of the Legendrian lift Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M of any nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M with stably trivial Gauss map is defined, and we denote it τ⁡(L)⊂H∗​(M,𝐑)\tau(L)\subset H^{*}(M;\mathbf{R}).
Furthermore, in [ACGK] a procedure for producing a generating function on a tube bundle for a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is given once the input of a nullhomotopy of the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O is fixed, using the doubling trick which Guillermou introduced in [Gui12]. We do not know whether any generating function on a tube bundle for a nearby Lagrangian is given by this procedure. We say that a generating function for LL which does arise by this procedure is natural and denote by ν⁡(L)⊂τ⁡(Λ)\nu(L)\subset\tau(\Lambda) the subset consisting of those higher torsion classes in τ⁡(Λ)\tau(\Lambda) of tube bundles W→MW\to M where the generating function for LL on WW is natural. We call ν⁡(L)\nu(L) the nearby Lagrangian torsion of LL. It satisfies the following properties:
Theorem 1.6.
Let L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M be a nearby Lagrangian with trivial stable Gauss map. The nearby Lagrangian torsion of LL satisfies the following:
(1)
ν⁡(L)\nu(L) is invariant under Hamiltonian isotopies of LL.
(2)
ν⁡(L)\nu(L) is a single coset of pp, so we get a well-defined element ν​(L)∈coker​(p)\nu(L)\in\text{coker}(p).
(3)
for the zero section we have ν​(M)=τ​(M)=im​(p)\nu(M)=\tau(M)=\text{im}(p).
Remark 1.7.
Although the tube torsion τ⁡(Λ)\tau(\Lambda) of the Legendrian lift Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M of a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is invariant under Legendrian isotopies of Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M, the nearby Lagrangian torsion ν⁡(L)\nu(L) is not obviously invariant under Legendrian isotopies of Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M. Concretely, if L1,L2⊂T∗​ML_{1},L_{2}\subset T^{*}M are two nearby Lagrangians with Legendrian isotopic Legendrian lifts, then we do not know whether it must be the case that ν⁡(L1)=ν⁡(L2)\nu(L_{1})=\nu(L_{2}), even though Theorem 1.4 guarantees that τ⁡(L1)=τ⁡(L2)\tau(L_{1})=\tau(L_{2}).
Example 1.8.
In [ACGK] it was also shown that the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O of a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is always trivial on homotopy groups. Since LL and MM are homotopy equivalent, this implies that L→U/OL\to U/O is always nullhomotopic when MM has the homotopy type of a sphere. So for nearby Lagrangian homotopy spheres, generating functions on tube bundles always exist and therefore the tube torsion and nearby Lagrangian torsion of a nearby Lagrangian homotopy sphere are always defined. Both invariants are automatically trivial for degree reasons unless the dimension of MM is of the form n=4​kn=4k. For concreteness, say M=S4​kM=S^{4k} is the standard sphere (though the discussion is similar if MM is any exotic sphere of dimension divisible by 4). The only possible nontrivial higher torsion class of a tube bundle W→S4​kW\to S^{4k} is τ2​k​(W)∈H4​k​(S4​k,𝐑)≃𝐑\tau_{2k}(W)\in H^{4k}(S^{4k};\mathbf{R})\simeq\mathbf{R}. Hence for a nearby Lagrangian homotopy sphere Σ⊂T∗​S4​k\Sigma\subset T^{*}S^{4k} we have a distinguished element
ν(Σ)∈coker(p:KO0(S4​k)→H4​k(S4​k;𝐑)).\nu(\Sigma)\in\text{coker}\left(p:KO^{0}(S^{4k})\to H^{4k}(S^{4k};\mathbf{R})\right).
Alternatively, we may view
ν⁡(Σ)∈coker​(𝐙→λk𝐑)=𝐑/λk​𝐙\nu(\Sigma)\in\text{coker}\left(\mathbf{Z}\xrightarrow{\lambda_{k}}\mathbf{R}\right)=\mathbf{R}/\lambda_{k}\mathbf{Z}

So the nearby Lagrangian torsion of any nearby Lagrangian homotopy sphere Σ⊂T∗​S4​k\Sigma\subset T^{*}S^{4k} is well-defined and it is just a real number modulo λk​𝐙\lambda_{k}\mathbf{Z}.
From [AD22] it is known that after a Hamiltonian isotopy we may assume that the front of any nearby Lagrangian homotopy sphere Σ⊂T∗​S4​k\Sigma\subset T^{*}S^{4k} only has cusp type singularities. A more precise version of this result will be stated and proved in Section 4 below.
Next, we introduce some terminology to distinguish from the case in which nearby Lagrangian torsion isn’t defined.
Definition 1.10.
We say that a Legendrian Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M has trivial tube torsion when τ​(Λ)=im​(p)\tau(\Lambda)=\text{im}(p). We say that a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M has trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion when ν​(L)=im​(p)\nu(L)=\text{im}(p).
Remark 1.11.
If a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M has trivial tube torsion, then it automatically has trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion.
We may formulate the resulting obstruction to Legendrian and Hamiltonian isotopy to the zero section as follows:
Corollary 1.12.
If a Legendrian Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M is Legendrian isotopic to the zero section, then it has trivial tube torsion. In particular, if a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section, then it has trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion.
The famous nearby Lagrangian conjecture states that any nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section. The following question is therefore natural.
Question 1.13.
Must a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M have trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion?
An affirmative answer to this question would provide further evidence towards the nearby Lagrangian conjecture, whereas a negative answer would disprove it. Note that according to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture the Legendrian lift Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M of a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M would in particular be Legendrian isotopic to MM, though even this weaker form of the conjecture is not known. It seems conceivable that there could exist a nearby Lagrangian with trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion but nontrivial tube torsion, which would also disprove the nearby Lagrangian conjecture.
Remark 1.14.
The invariant ν⁡(L)\nu(L) is an invariant of a single nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M. It is a parametrized torsion invariant of a family of acyclic chain complexes associated to LL. The space of parameters is MM, and for a single parameter m∈Mm\in M the relevant chain complex is (at least conjecturally) C​F∗​(Tm​M,L)CF^{*}(T_{m}M,L), see Section 4.5. However, we take the generating function viewpoint in the present article and use the fiberwise Morse complex C∗​(fm)C_{*}(f_{m}) of a natural generating function ff for LL instead. The work by Courte and Porcelli [CP25] gives a vanishing result for the parametrized higher torsion of a family of nearby Lagrangians Lz⊂T∗​ML_{z}\subset T^{*}M,z∈Zz\in Z, where for a single parameter the relevant chain complex is C​F∗​(M,Lz)CF^{*}(M,L_{z}) for M⊂T∗​MM\subset T^{*}M the zero section, though [CP25] also takes the viewpoint of generating functions. The work [CP25] is closer to a parametric generalization of the result [AK] of vanishing of Whitehead torsion for a single nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M, which concerns C​F∗​(M,L)CF^{*}(M,L). Indeed, the invariants τ⁡(L)\tau(L) and ν⁡(L)\nu(L) have no non-parametric analogue; the fiber of a tube bundle is simply connected so its Whitehead group is trivial. It’s possible the two viewpoints may be reconciled by some assembly type map.
In the broader class of Legendrians which are not necessarily lifts of nearby Lagrangians, we show that the theory of tube torsion is nontrivial in that Legendrians with nontrivial tube torsion abound. In fact, we establish the existence of Legendrians which have nontrivial tube torsion and which are diffeomorphic to the base, so that the conjectural triviality of tube torsion for nearby Lagrangians would in any case not follow from known constraints on the topology of nearby Lagrangians.
To formulate the precise statement, we will use the viewpoint of Waldhausen [Wal82] where a fibration sequence ℋ∞→𝒯∞→B​G\mathcal{H}_{\infty}\to\mathcal{T}_{\infty}\to BG is constructed. Here ℋ∞\mathcal{H}_{\infty} is the space of stable h-cobordisms of a point (which classifies bundles of h-cobordisms of a disk up to stable equivalence), 𝒯∞\mathcal{T}_{\infty} is the stable space of tubes (which classifies tube bundles up to stable equivalence), and B​GBG is the classifying space for stable spherical fibrations, so G=limnGnG=\lim_{n}G_{n} for GnG_{n} the space of self homotopy-equivalences of SnS^{n}. In particular, this means given a bundle H→V→MH\to V\to M of h-cobordisms of a disk, one may attach VV to a trivial tube bundle M×TM\times T, where TT is the standard tube, to obtain a tube bundle T→W→MT\to W\to M. The tube bundle WW has the same higher torsion as VV.
Theorem 1.15.
Let H→V→MH\to V\to M be a bundle of hh-cobordisms of a disk and let T→W→MT\to W\to M the resulting tube bundle. There exists a Legendrian Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M which admits a generating function on WW and whose projection to the base Λ→M\Lambda\to M is homotopic to a diffeomorphism. In particular the higher torsion classes τk​(V)∈H2​k​(M,𝐑)\tau_{k}(V)\in H^{2k}(M;\mathbf{R}) of VV are contained in the tube torsion τ⁡(Λ)⊂H∗​(M,𝐑)\tau(\Lambda)\subset H^{*}(M;\mathbf{R}) of Λ\Lambda.
The higher torsion of tube bundles arising from h-cobordism bundles as in Theorem 1.15 is in general not contained in the image of the (normalized) Pontryagin character, and hence this result shows that Legendrians with nontrivial tube torsion exist in abundance. Unfortunately, we do not know how to visualize a single explicit example of a Legendrian with nontrivial tube torsion. The simplest possible example would live in J1​S4J^{1}S^{4}.
Problem 1.16.
Describe explicitly, or draw the front of a Legendrian in J1​S4J^{1}S^{4} with nontrivial tube torsion.
Although we do not know whether nearby Lagrangians must always have trivial tube torsion, or even whether they must always have trivial nearby Lagrangian torsion, in the upcoming work [AIS] we will prove the triviality of nearby Lagrangian torsion under the additional assumption that the front admits a ruling satisfying certain technical conditions, which we call a restricted ruling.
Finally we note that if a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M has a stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O which is not nullhomotopic, then it cannot admit any generating function, so that tube torsion is not defined. However, such an LL would already be a counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture, since a Hamiltonian isotopy between LL and the zero section would in particular yield a nullhomotopy of the stable Gauss map.

purpose: Natural torsion coset versus arbitrary generating family
text:
The existence theorem for generating functions of tube type from [ACGK] is proved by a construction which is canonical once a nullhomotopy of the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O is fixed. We will now show that this construction picks out a distinguished coset ν⁡(L)⊂τ⁡(L)\nu(L)\subset\tau(L) of im​(p)\text{im}(p) which will turn out to be invariant under Hamiltonian isotopies of LL, though not obviously so under Legendrian isotopies of the Legendrian lift of LL.
4.2. The Guillermou trick
The following result is implicit in [ACGK].
Proposition 4.4.
Let L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M be a nearby Lagrangian with trivial stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O. The doubling construction determines a distinguished coset of the rigid tube map [M,B​O]→[M,𝒯∞][M,BO]\to[M,\mathcal{T}_{\infty}] which is invariant under Hamiltonian isotopy of LL.
Indeed, [ACGK] identifies the colimit of the left action of stabilization by x2−y2x^{2}-y^{2} on 𝒯\mathcal{T} as the space 𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty}. This colimit still has a right action of 𝒬\mathcal{Q}, so we may form the (geometric realization) of the bar construction B⁡(𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞,𝒬)B(\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty},\mathcal{Q}). To any nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M the (twisted) doubling construction associates a homotopy class of map M→B⁡(𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞,𝒬)M\to B(\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty},\mathcal{Q}), invariant under Hamiltonian isotopy of LL (this map classifies a twisted generating function). We have a fibration sequence by Diagram 4.2 of [ACGK] which reads
𝐙×B​O→𝐙×𝒯∞→B⁡(𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞,𝒬)→U/O\mathbf{Z}\times BO\to\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty}\to B(\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty},\mathcal{Q})\to U/O
and such that the composition M→B⁡(𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞,𝒬)→U/OM\to B(\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty},\mathcal{Q})\to U/O is the stable Gauss map of LL under a homotopy inverse for the projection L→ML\to M. So the desired statement follows formally from the fact that a nullhomotopy of M→U/OM\to U/O is equivalent to a lift M→𝐙×𝒯∞M\to\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty} of the map M→B⁡(𝐙×𝐙×𝒯∞,𝒬)M\to B(\mathbf{Z}\times\mathbf{Z}\times\mathcal{T}_{\infty},\mathcal{Q}), which is homotopically unique up to a lift M→𝐙×B​OM\to\mathbf{Z}\times BO. In fact, if we know a priori that LL has trivial stable Gauss map we may avoid the bar construction and we briefly explain how this works.
Given a Legendrian submanifold Λ⊂J1​M\Lambda\subset J^{1}M, a local generating function for Λ\Lambda consists of a generating function f:U→𝐑f:U\to\mathbf{R} where U⊂M×𝐑NU\subset M\times\mathbf{R}^{N} is some open subset. Since UU could be an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the fiberwise singular set of ff this notion amounts to a purely linear algebraic question. Indeed, as discussed in Section 2.4 it goes back to Giroux [G90] that the existence of a so-called local generating function is equivalent to the triviality of the stable Gauss map Λ→U/O\Lambda\to U/O. Moreover, as is explained in [G90] and further discussed in [ACGK], one may take as input a nullhomotopy of the stable Gauss map Λ→U/O\Lambda\to U/O to construct such a local generating function. If one were to change the chosen null-homotopy of the stable Gauss map by concatenating with a map Λ→Ω⁡(U/O),\Lambda\to\Omega(U/O), then this would correspond to performing a twisted stabilization of the local generating function by a family of quadratic forms on Λ.\Lambda. The negative eigenspaces of the fiberwise Hessian form a real vector bundle EE over Λ\Lambda classified by the map Λ→𝐙×B​O\Lambda\to\mathbf{Z}\times BO corresponding to the given map Λ→Ω⁡(U/O)\Lambda\to\Omega(U/O) under the model for Bott periodicity Ω⁡(U/O)≃𝐙×B​O\Omega(U/O)\simeq\mathbf{Z}\times BO considered in [G90].
The construction for generating functions of tube type for nearby Lagrangians L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M with trivial stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O takes a nullhomotopy of the Gauss map and the corresponding local generating function f:U→𝐑f:U\to\mathbf{R} where U⊂M×𝐑N+1U\subset M\times\mathbf{R}^{N+1} as its starting point, and then argues as follows. Denote 𝐑N+1=𝐑×𝐑\mathbf{R}^{N+1}=\mathbf{R}\times\mathbf{R} with x∈𝐑x\in\mathbf{R} the coordinate of the second factor. By a direct sum with the function x3+3​xx^{3}+3x one may construct a local generating function for a double of Λ\Lambda, which consists of two parallel copies of Λ\Lambda in J1​MJ^{1}M, namely Λ0​∐Λ1\Lambda_{0}\coprod\Lambda_{1} for Λ0=Λ\Lambda_{0}=\Lambda and Λϵ\Lambda_{\epsilon} a shift of Λ\Lambda by a small but constant amount ϵ∈𝐑+\epsilon\in\mathbf{R}_{+} in the zz-coordinate J1​M=T∗​M×𝐑zJ^{1}M=T^{*}M\times\mathbf{R}_{z}. Further, by a judicious choice of cutoffs, one may arrange for the double of Λ\Lambda to be generated by a global, i.e. not local, generating function hs:M×𝐑N+1→𝐑h_{s}:M\times\mathbf{R}^{N+1}\to\mathbf{R} such that away from the critical set there holds ∂h/∂x≠0\partial h/\partial x\neq 0 for the distinguished coordinate xx of 𝐑N+1=𝐑N×𝐑\mathbf{R}^{N+1}=\mathbf{R}^{N}\times\mathbf{R}.
When Λ\Lambda happens to be the Legendrian lift of a nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M, one may use the following remarkable trick due to Guillermou [Gui12]. Consider the family Λ0​∐Λs\Lambda_{0}\coprod\Lambda_{s} as s>0s>0 gets larger. Since LL is an embedded Lagrangian, Λ\Lambda has no Reeb chords and hence Λ0​∐Λs⊂J1​M\Lambda_{0}\coprod\Lambda_{s}\subset J^{1}M is a Legendrian isotopy. Possibly after increasing NN, by the homotopy lifting property for generating functions there continues to exists a family of functions hs:M×𝐑N→𝐑h_{s}:M\times\mathbf{R}^{N}\to\mathbf{R} generating Λ0​∐Λs\Lambda_{0}\coprod\Lambda_{s} such that ∂hs/∂x≠0\partial h_{s}/\partial x\neq 0 outside of a compact subset. When s=Ts=T is big enough so that there exists a value c∈𝐑c\in\mathbf{R} such that the zz-coordinate of Λ\Lambda is always below cc and the zz-coordinate for ΛT\Lambda_{T} is always above cc, we may consider the codimension zero sub-bundle {hT≤c}⊂M×𝐑N\{h_{T}\leq c\}\subset M\times\mathbf{R}^{N}. It is shown in [ACGK] that the resulting fiber bundle is a bundle of tubes in a sense which is close to Waldhausen’s parition model 𝒯N,kp\mathcal{T}_{N,k}^{p}, which stably has the same homotopy type as the space of functions of tube types 𝒯N,k\mathcal{T}_{N,k} in the sense of the present article as discussed in Section 3.6. The homotopy class of the resulting map M→𝒯∞M\to\mathcal{T}_{\infty} only depends on the choice of nullhomotopy of the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O.
The monoid [M,Ω⁡(U/O)][M,\Omega(U/O)] (with respect to concatenation of loops in Ω⁡(U/O)\Omega(U/O)) acts transitively on the set of homotopy classes of nullhomotopies of the stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O of any nearby Lagrangian L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M, since we may concatenate any such nullhomotopy with the resulting map L→M→Ω⁡(U/O)L\to M\to\Omega(U/O). As discussed above, the effect on the resulting class in [M,𝒯∞][M,\mathcal{T}_{\infty}] is given by the action of [M,B​O][M,BO] with respect to the twisted stabilization, i.e. with respect to the rigid tube map B​O→𝒯∞BO\to\mathcal{T}_{\infty}, under the model for Bott periodicity Ω⁡(U/O)≃𝐙×B​O\Omega(U/O)\simeq\mathbf{Z}\times BO of [G90].
Finally, the doubling construction works parametrically, as long as the path of Lagrangians is covered by a homotopy of null-homotopies of the stable Gauss map, so the resulting coset of the map [M,B​O]→[M,𝒯∞][M,BO]\to[M,\mathcal{T}_{\infty}] is a Hamiltonian isotopy invariant.
Definition 4.5.
The coset of the map [M,B​O]→[M,𝒯∞][M,BO]\to[M,\mathcal{T}_{\infty}] distinguished by Proposition 4.4 is be called the natural coset.
Definition 4.6.
Let L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M be a nearby Lagrangian with trivial stable Gauss map L→U/OL\to U/O. The nearby Lagrangian torsion ν⁡(L)⊂τ⁡(L)\nu(L)\subset\tau(L) is the subset of H∗​(M,𝐑)H^{*}(M;\mathbf{R}) consisting of the (negatives of the) higher torsion classes of tube bundles in the natural coset of LL.

Let L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M be a nearby Lagrangian generated by a generating function of tube type f:M×𝐑N→𝐑f:M\times\mathbf{R}^{N}\to\mathbf{R}. We say that ff is natural if it arises from the doubling construction.
Remark 4.8.
To be precise, this means that the doubling construction of [ACGK] produces a generating function gg for LL which is of tube type in the sense of [ACGK] and such that via the modification of [AACK] the function gg corresponds to ff. So ff is a fibered function of tube type in the sense of the present article. Note that ff being natural implies, but is not a priori equivalent to, that the tube bundle W=T⁡(f)W=T(f) is in the natural coset of the rigid tube map.
Remark 4.9.
For i=0,1i=0,1 let Li⊂T∗​ML_{i}\subset T^{*}M be a nearby Lagrangian and let Λi⊂J1​M\Lambda_{i}\subset J^{1}M be corresponding Legendrian lifts. It could in principle be possible that L0L_{0} and L1L_{1} are not Hamiltonian isotopic but Λ0\Lambda_{0} and Λ1\Lambda_{1} are Legendrian isotopic. If so, then τ⁡(Λ0)=τ⁡(Λ1)\tau(\Lambda_{0})=\tau(\Lambda_{1}), i.e. their tube torsions agree. However the authors do not know whether tube torsion need be a single pp-coset, in principle it could be larger. In particular it could be the case that ν⁡(L0)≠ν⁡(L1)\nu(L_{0})\neq\nu(L_{1}), i.e. that the nearby Lagrangian torsion pp-cosets are different, even though the (larger) collections of pp-cosets τ⁡(Λ0)=τ⁡(Λ1)\tau(\Lambda_{0})=\tau(\Lambda_{1}) coincide.
4.3. Nearby Lagrangians with moderate tangencies
Suppose that L⊂T∗​ML\subset T^{*}M is a nearby Lagrangian whose projection L→ML\to M only has fold type singularities, or equivalently such that the Legendrian front (of Legendrian lift) of LL in J0​M=M×𝐑J^{0}M=M\times\mathbf{R} only has cusp singularities. Yet another equivalent condition is that LL has quadratic tangencies with respect to the foliation of T∗​MT^{*}M by the cotangent leaves Tm∗​MT_{m}^{*}M, m∈Mm\in M, see Figure 1.
